role.altitude: The producer or director keeps choosing locations, judging dailies and negotiating deals; reports, call sheets, script mailings and term comparisons by hand shrink.
skills_to_grow: Keeping schedules, contacts and rights records in one planning tool
role.ambitious_version: A producer whose call sheets and reports run themselves, with the week spent on deals and the set.

tasks.short: Brief the location scout, review candidate locations, visit the shortlist, choose settings and locations for films, decide how scenes will be shot there and record the choice for the crew.

steps.what: Director briefs the location scout on what each scene needs
Location scout searches for and photographs candidate locations
Director reviews location photos and makes a shortlist
Director visits shortlisted locations with the director of photography and heads of department
Director chooses the settings and locations and determines how scenes will be shot in them
Director writes up the chosen location and shooting notes per scene for the crew

tasks.design: The location brief comes from the scene breakdown in the production planning tool ({PROJECT}), and the scout's photos land in a shared location gallery tagged by scene instead of mail attachments. After the recce the director records the choice and shooting notes against each scene with the recce photos, so the crew read them in one place. Scouting, visits and the choice stay with people.
tasks.previous_blocker: Briefs, photos and notes travelled by mail and were retyped into documents.
tasks.enabler_now: Planning tools hold scene-linked galleries and notes shared with freelancers.
tasks.still_hard: Every judgement about light, space and sound on site.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing how a place will look on camera.
tasks.altitude: Little changes; less time goes into mail and write-ups.

reach.learn: Whether scene-linked location notes cut questions before the shoot.

evidence.claim: Production planning tools share scene-linked galleries and notes with freelancers.

assumptions: Boundary: from the location brief to the location plan for the crew; permits and location contracts are outside.
Input contract for s1: the scene breakdown in the planning tool; fallback is a written brief.
The scout uploads photos to the gallery; the scout's own time is supplier labour and does not change.
Visits and the choice keep their full time.
research_questions: Do crew ask fewer location questions with scene-linked notes?

already_counted.description: Director links recce photos and notes to scenes in the planning tool.

incremental.description: Director tags gallery photos to scenes.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: one or two locations chosen in a single recce; high: a production with many locations and long mail threads with the scout.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Have the dailies prepared, review film daily, note selected takes and problems, discuss changes with the team and update the plan for future filming.

steps.what: Editor or data technician syncs sound and uploads the day's footage as dailies
Director reviews film daily to check on work in progress
Director notes selected takes, problems and needed pickups on paper
Director discusses changes for future filming with the director of photography, editor and producer
Director plans future filming by adding pickups and changes to the shot list

tasks.design: A dailies system ({OTHER}) syncs sound and posts the day's clips, and the director adds marks and notes on the clip timecode while watching instead of on paper, so the editor gets them attached to the actual clips. Pickups marked in the notes are added to the shot list in the planning tool ({PROJECT}); watching and the team discussion stay as they are.
tasks.previous_blocker: Notes on paper had to be matched to clips by the editor.
tasks.enabler_now: Dailies viewers take notes on timecode and share them with the editor.
tasks.still_hard: Judging performance and picture is the whole task.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing in the dailies what the scene still lacks.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes in the director's decisions; notes reach the editor attached to clips.

reach.learn: Whether timecoded notes shorten the assembly.

evidence.claim: Dailies viewers let reviewers attach notes to timecodes and share them with the editor.

assumptions: Boundary: from dailies prepared to the updated shot list; editing is outside.
Input contract for s3: clips in the dailies system with timecodes from the camera files; fallback is paper notes.
The editor's sync time is other-role labour and outside the director's savings.
Watching and the discussion keep their full time.
unknowns: Whether the production uses a dailies system.
research_questions: Do fewer takes get lost between dailies and edit?

already_counted.description: Director checks that timecoded notes sit on the right clips before the editor starts.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: short dailies with few notes; high: long shooting days with many takes and pickups.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prepare the deal from the rights record, negotiate with independent producers, distributors and broadcasters, exchange term sheets, compare the final contract with the agreed terms, get it signed off and send it for signature.

steps.what: Producer prepares the deal: rights to offer, territories, windows and price expectations
Producer negotiates with independent producers, distributors and broadcasters in meetings and calls
Producer writes and exchanges offers and term sheets by e-mail
Business affairs drafts and negotiates the contract from the term sheet
Producer reviews the final contract against the agreed terms

loop.input: The final contract text and the term sheet fields (rights, territories, windows, fees, delivery dates).
loop.output: A table per term: the contract clause, the value it states and whether it matches the term sheet.
loop.check: Every extracted value must quote the clause it comes from, or the term is marked 'not found'; the producer reads every clause marked different or not found.
loop.why_not_simpler: Counterparties send contracts on their own paper, so terms are not in fixed places.

steps.what: Managing director approves and signs the final contract
Producer sends the signed contract to the counterparty for signature

approvals.approved_version: final contract as approved and signed by the managing director in s6; the e-signature envelope carries that file and any change voids it

tasks.design: A rights records app shows which rights, territories and windows are still free from signed contracts, so the deal position is read rather than rebuilt. Term sheets are filled from that record and the agreed terms; when the final contract arrives on the counterparty's paper, a bounded step lists each term with its clause and whether it matches the term sheet, and the producer reads every difference. Negotiating stays with the producer and the contract with business affairs; after the managing director signs, the {ESIGN} platform sends exactly that file.
tasks.previous_blocker: Rights held were tracked in spreadsheets per production, and contracts were compared with term sheets by reading.
tasks.enabler_now: Rights records apps are standard configuration; language models extract terms from contracts with clause quotes.
tasks.still_hard: The negotiation itself and judging what a buyer will pay.
tasks.human_edge: Reading the other side and knowing when to walk away.
tasks.altitude: The producer spends deal time on negotiation instead of lookups and comparisons; decision rights do not change.

reach.learn: Which terms differ most often between term sheet and contract.

evidence.claim: Language models can extract stated terms from contracts and quote the clause for each.
Commercial broadcasters must give at least 50% of programming to European works and 10% to independent works, which shapes what buyers ask for.

assumptions: Boundary: from the deal position to the contract sent for signature; delivery of the production is outside.
Input contract for s1: rights, territories and windows entered from each signed contract by business affairs; fallback is the contract files.
Input contract for s5: the term sheet fields from s3 and the final contract as text; scanned contracts are read by hand.
Negotiation, business affairs work and the managing director's approval do not change.
unknowns: Number of deals per year and how many are on the counterparty's paper.
Whether rights records exist outside spreadsheets.
research_questions: How many contract differences does the comparison find that reading missed?
Does the rights record prevent double sales of a window?

already_counted.description: Producer reads clauses marked different or not found.
Producer checks the rights record for the deal.

incremental.description: Producer adds agreed deal terms to the rights record after signature.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: a single broadcaster deal on the company's own contract template; high: a catalogue sold to many distributors on their own paper.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prepare operational reports, write rehearsal call sheets, send them, release script copies to cast and crew, and arrange rehearsal quarters.

steps.what: Producer prepares operational reports on progress, spend against budget and hours
Producer writes the rehearsal call sheets with times, place, cast and crew and checks the final version
Producer distributes the rehearsal call sheets to cast and crew
Producer checks which script version to release and who receives it
Producer distributes script copies to cast and crew
Producer arranges rehearsal quarters: finds a free room, books it and confirms

approvals.approved_version: call sheet for that rehearsal day as checked by the producer in s2; a schedule change makes a new version that needs a new check
script version and recipient list confirmed by the producer in s4; each copy is watermarked with its recipient

tasks.design: The production planning tool ({PROJECT}) holds the rehearsal schedule and cast and crew contacts; call sheets are generated from them, the producer checks the final version, and the tool sends it. Script copies of the version the producer releases go out watermarked per recipient. An operational report dashboard in {BI} shows scenes actually rehearsed or shot from the production reports and spend from {ERP} postings against budget; booking rehearsal rooms stays a phone and mail job, helped by a venue list with contacts and past rates.
tasks.previous_blocker: Call sheets and script mailings were assembled by hand from schedules and contact lists in different files.
tasks.enabler_now: Production tools generate call sheets from the schedule and send them.
tasks.still_hard: Finding a free rehearsal room at short notice.
tasks.human_edge: Keeping cast and crew on the same page when plans change.
tasks.altitude: The producer's admin hours shrink; decision rights do not change.

reach.task: Issue daily call sheets on set
reach.learn: How often call sheets change after sending.

evidence.claim: A production tool produces call sheets, schedules and budgets.
Cast and crew contact details are personal data and may be shared only for the production.

assumptions: Boundary: from production data to reports, call sheets, script copies and rooms booked; the rehearsals themselves are outside.

Input contract for s1: production reports of scenes actually rehearsed or shot, entered by the assistant director each day; spend from ledger postings coded to the production; the report shows actuals, not the plan.
Input contract for s2: the rehearsal schedule and cast and crew contacts kept in the planning tool by the producer; fallback is a template filled by hand.
Cast and crew are treated as the production team, so call sheets and scripts are internal sends; each still goes out only in the checked version.
Booking rooms keeps most of its time.
unknowns: How many rehearsal days per production.
Whether the production already uses a planning tool.
research_questions: How many call sheet versions are sent per day before and after?
Do script leaks fall with watermarked copies?

already_counted.description: Producer reads the report dashboard and writes comments.
Producer checks each generated call sheet and adds notes.

incremental.description: Producer keeps contacts, schedule and templates in the planning tool current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: a small production that keeps contacts in mail and rehearses in one fixed room; high: a large cast production with daily call sheets and frequent script revisions.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
